posts.text:
A Hong Kong-based company needed two senior React engineers before peak season. Hiring locally meant 60–90 days and $150K+ a year per engineer.

They run a digital marketplace that connects shipping companies with logistics operators. Their checkout was outdated, and conversion was stalling while competitors launched sleeker platforms.

We screened for more than React:
- Next.js depth, tested with a coding challenge.
- A UX case study: walk us through a feature you shipped, what it did for users, and how you measured it.
- A/B testing and conversion experience.
- How clearly each candidate explains technical decisions.

Result: three candidates shortlisted in nine days, two offers accepted, and both engineers productive within 30 days.

In the first 90 days, checkout conversion rose from 4.2% to 4.96%, and A/B testing went from 2 tests a quarter to 4–5 a month.

One detail I like: Hong Kong is only an hour ahead of Jakarta, and the engineers still worked async-first, writing updates and recording decisions. A close time zone doesn't make writing things down optional.

They were hired through our Employer of Record, so the client needed no Indonesian entity.

The full case study:
https://lnkd.in/gfphhjpA

In today's competitive landscape, understanding customer satisfaction in real time is crucial for business growth. To address this, I built a complete, microservice-based web application that automatically analyzes customer reviews and computes real-time sentiment metrics.
🏗️System Architecture & Key Features:
🔹 AI Sentiment Analysis Microservice (Python & FastAPI):
Integrated NLP (Natural Language Processing) using NLTK's VADER model to calculate compound polarity scores (-1.0 to +1.0) and categorize reviews intoPositive, Neutral, and Negative.
🔹 Enterprise Backend Core (Spring Boot & Java 21):
Designed RESTful APIs using Spring Data JPA, Hibernate, and MySQL. Implemented robust fault tolerance with fallback mechanisms, bean validations (Jakarta Validation), global exception handling, and database indexing for high performance.
🔹 Interactive Dashboard UI (React & TypeScript):
Developed a modern, responsive user interface featuring dynamic sentiment distribution charts, real-time analytics, and smooth hover interactions.
🔹 Full-Stack Microservices Integration:
Decoupled services communicating via synchronous REST calls with automated service-to-service integration and one-click deployment workflows.
🛠️ Tech Stack:
• Frontend: React.js, TypeScript, HTML5/CSS3
 • Backend: Java 21, Spring Boot, Spring Data JPA, Hibernate

I'm hiring a Human Capital Business Partner Manager atMaison Feerie to support our operations across Surabaya and Jakarta.

What I find interesting about this role is how varied the work is. You might help our departments leader work through a performance issue, review an agreement with a business partner, or plan the hires needed for an upcoming opening. You’ll work directly with Department Heads and Store Leaders, so your advice needs to be practical enough for them to act on.

The role focuses on four areas.
1. Legal. Review employment contracts, company policies, and third-party agreements, including agreements with mall operators. Advise management on legal risks and how to address them in day-to-day decisions.
2. Industrial Relations. Work with operational leaders to handle employee grievances, disciplinary cases, and disputes. You’ll need a practical understanding of Indonesian employment law, particularlyUU No. 27 Tahun 2026 tentang Pelindungan Ketenagakerjaan.
3. Performance Management. Help Department Heads set KPIs that their teams can measure consistently. Review the data and supporting evidence with them, identify performance gaps, and agree on what to follow up.
4. Talent Acquisition & Employer Branding. Lead recruitment from sourcing through offer, build a pipeline for key roles, and give candidates a clear picture of the work and culture at Maison Féerie.

ABachelor’s degree in Law (S1 Hukum) is mandatory, and having an advocate license would be an advantage, along withat least five (5) years of HR business partnering experience. Experience in F&B, retail, hospitality, or another multi-outlet business is a plus.

If this sounds like work you’d enjoy, feel free to message me here on LinkedIn. I’d be happy to share more about the role and the team. If someone in your network comes to mind, please pass this along.

posts.text:
In Indonesia, shopping spikes follow content, not just calendars. The Ministry of Trade reported that during Harbolnas 2025, 54% of consumers shopped through creator affiliate links and 80% used livestream features.

On Tokopedia and TikTok Shop’s 10.10 promo this year, transactions rose 9x and 4x respectively, according to the platforms.

For anyone running an online store, that changes how you plan for peak days:

• A spike can start in seconds, when a creator goes live or a flash sale opens, not on a schedule

• It doesn’t peak once. It peaks in waves, all day

• The checkout page takes the hit, not the product page

Three things that help:

1. Scale on demand, not on a timetable: auto-scaling that reacts in minutes, and is tested before the day
2. Protect checkout: queues and rate limits, so a wave slows people down instead of breaking things
3. Cache what you can: product pages, images and search results, ahead of the spike

If a creator sold out 10,000 units in ten minutes, what would happen to your checkout?

The most compelling aspect of this year’s curriculum is how Pijak integrates AI literacy with hands-on experience in building web applications using IBM Agentic Coding (with JavaScript and React), complemented by soft skills training such as public speaking and job interview preparation. This opportunity is open to:
🔹 General/Professional Track: Indonesian citizens aged 18–34 (job seekers, early-career professionals, or those looking to make a career switch) who are not currently enrolled in formal education.
🔹 Student/Vocational Track: Active vocational high school (SMK) students and vocational education students (D1–D4) in Indonesia.
